title: Lineal World Boxing Champions
intro: The lineal champion is the fighter who beat the fighter: one line of succession, instead of four sanctioning bodies each crowning a different man.
why: Boxing has four world titles per division (WBA, WBC, IBF, WBO), so "world champion" alone can mean four different people at once. The lineal championship follows one line: it changes hands only in the ring, and when a champion retires or moves up, it falls vacant until two leading contenders settle it.

divisions.name: Heavyweight
divisions.note: The most continuous lineage in the sport. The title was vacant between Vitali Klitschko's 2004 retirement and Wladimir Klitschko's 2009 claim.

divisions.name: Light heavyweight
divisions.note: ⚠️ The most contested lineage of the four. The line broke when Michael Spinks moved up to heavyweight in 1985, and sources disagree on how it resumed — Ring Magazine traces it through Roy Jones Jr, the Cyber Boxing Zone through Virgil Hill. This table lists only the reigns we could verify, and is deliberately incomplete rather than filled in with a disputed lineage.
rows: First undisputed champion of the four-belt era
Unified WBC, WBA and IBF by 1999; vacated to fight at heavyweight
Michael Spinks moved up to heavyweight

divisions.name: Middleweight
divisions.note: Vacant for long stretches — after Sugar Ray Leonard's 1987 retirement, after James Toney vacated in 1993, and again after Canelo Álvarez moved up.
rows: Beat Gennadiy Golovkin in the 2018 rematch; later moved up
Took the title from Alan Minter, 27 September 1980

divisions.name: Lightweight
divisions.note: Gaps at 2012–2014, 2015–2020 and from 2023, when the champion moved up in weight and no successor bout settled the line.
